items.meaning: to search for information in a dictionary, online, etc.
items.example: If you don't know a word, look it up.

items.meaning: to try to find something or someone
items.example: I'm looking for my keys. Have you seen them?

items.meaning: to take care of someone or something
items.example: Can you look after my dog this weekend?

items.meaning: to feel happy and excited about something that is going to happen
items.example: I'm really looking forward to the summer holidays.

items.meaning: to be careful (often used as a warning)
items.example: Look out! There's a car coming.

items.meaning: to investigate or examine a problem
items.example: The manager promised to look into my complaint.

items.meaning: to check something quickly
items.example: Could you look over my CV before I send it?

items.meaning: to think you are better than someone
items.example: Don't look down on people who earn less than you.

items.meaning: to get out of bed
items.example: I get up at seven every day.

items.meaning: to return to a place
items.example: What time did you get back last night?

items.meaning: to have a friendly relationship with someone
items.example: Do you get on with your neighbours?

items.meaning: to recover from an illness or a bad experience
items.example: It took her months to get over the break-up.

items.meaning: to meet socially
items.example: Let's get together for dinner next week.

items.meaning: to manage to deal with a difficult period; to reach someone by phone
items.translation: superar (un mal momento) / contactar por teléfono
items.example: I tried to call the bank, but I couldn't get through.

items.meaning: to avoid doing something you don't want to do
items.example: He always gets out of washing the dishes.

items.meaning: to have just enough money or knowledge to live or do something
items.example: My Italian isn't great, but I can get by.

items.meaning: to do something wrong without being punished
items.example: He cheated in the exam and got away with it.

items.meaning: to remove a piece of clothing; (a plane) to leave the ground
items.example: Take your shoes off, please.

items.meaning: to start doing a new hobby or activity
items.example: She took up yoga last year.

items.meaning: to look or behave like an older family member
items.example: He takes after his father: they both love football.

items.meaning: to invite someone to a restaurant, cinema, etc. and pay
items.example: He took her out for dinner on her birthday.

items.meaning: to admit that something you said was wrong; to return something to a shop
items.example: I'm sorry, I take it back.

items.meaning: to take control of something
items.example: A big company took over the business.

items.meaning: to accept work or responsibility; to employ someone
items.example: The shop is taking on new staff for Christmas.

items.meaning: to deceive someone; to understand something
items.example: Don't be taken in by their cheap offers.

items.meaning: to stop doing something
items.example: My grandfather gave up smoking ten years ago.

items.meaning: to return something to its owner
items.example: Can you give me back my pen?

items.meaning: to give something for free; to tell a secret
items.example: Don't give away the ending of the film!

items.meaning: to give something to many people
items.example: The teacher gave out the exams.

items.meaning: to finally agree to something after refusing
items.example: The kids kept asking until their parents gave in.

items.meaning: to start a machine or a light
items.example: Can you turn on the light?

items.meaning: to stop a machine or a light
items.example: Turn it off before you leave.

items.meaning: to increase the volume or temperature; to arrive
items.example: Turn up the music, I love this song!

items.meaning: to refuse an offer; to reduce the volume
items.example: She turned down the job offer.

items.meaning: to move so you face the opposite direction; to make something improve
items.translation: darse la vuelta / dar un giro
items.example: Turn around and look at the camera.

items.meaning: to change and become something different
items.example: The small café turned into a famous restaurant.

items.meaning: to happen or end in a particular way
items.example: The party turned out to be really fun.

items.meaning: to dress yourself in a piece of clothing
items.example: Put on your coat, it's cold.

items.meaning: to put something in the place where it is usually kept
items.example: Put your toys away, please.

items.meaning: to delay something until later
items.example: Stop putting off your homework!

items.meaning: to stop a fire or a cigarette from burning
items.example: The firefighters put out the fire quickly.

items.meaning: to build or raise something; to let someone stay in your home
items.example: We put up the tent before it got dark.

items.meaning: to write something; to criticise someone
items.example: He always puts his sister down in front of others.

items.meaning: to connect someone on the phone
items.example: Please hold, I'll put you through to the manager.

items.meaning: to accept an annoying situation or person
items.example: I can't put up with this noise any more.

items.meaning: to enter a room or building
items.example: Come in and sit down.

items.meaning: to return to a place
items.example: Come back soon!

items.meaning: to visit someone at their home
items.example: Why don't you come over for coffee?

items.meaning: to be mentioned or discussed; to happen unexpectedly
items.example: Your name came up in the meeting.

items.meaning: to think of an idea or a plan
items.example: She came up with a great idea for the party.

items.meaning: to find something or meet someone by chance
items.example: I came across some old photos in the attic.

items.meaning: to start to have an illness
items.example: I think I'm coming down with a cold.

items.meaning: to leave home to enjoy yourself; (a light or fire) to stop burning
items.example: Do you want to go out tonight?

items.meaning: to return to a place
items.example: I'd love to go back to Rome one day.

items.meaning: to continue
items.example: The meeting went on for three hours.

items.meaning: to increase
items.example: The price of petrol went up again.

items.meaning: to decrease
items.example: The number of tourists went down last year.

items.meaning: (an alarm) to ring; (food) to become bad; (a bomb) to explode
items.example: My alarm went off at six.

items.meaning: to start or continue doing something
items.example: We finally got permission to go ahead with the new building.

items.meaning: to check or review something carefully
items.example: Let's go over the plan one more time.

items.meaning: to experience something difficult
items.example: She went through a hard time after losing her job.

items.meaning: to look good together; to match
items.example: Does this tie go with my shirt?

items.meaning: to escape from a place or person
items.example: The dog ran away when it heard the fireworks.

items.meaning: to have no more of something
items.example: We've run out of milk.

items.meaning: to meet someone by chance
items.example: I ran into an old friend at the supermarket.

items.meaning: to hit someone or something with a vehicle
items.example: Be careful not to run over the cat.

items.meaning: to lift something; to collect someone in a car
items.example: I'll pick you up at the station at six.

items.meaning: to choose something or someone from a group
items.example: Pick out the dress you like best.

items.meaning: to criticise or tease someone unfairly
items.example: Stop picking on your little brother!

items.meaning: to stop working (a machine or a car); to start crying
items.example: Our car broke down on the motorway.

items.meaning: to end a romantic relationship
items.example: They broke up after five years together.

items.meaning: to enter a building illegally, usually to steal
items.example: Someone broke into our house last night.

items.meaning: to start suddenly (a fire, a war, a disease)
items.example: A fire broke out in the kitchen.

items.meaning: to end something suddenly, such as a relationship or a conversation
items.example: They broke off their engagement a month before the wedding.

items.meaning: to raise a child; to start talking about a subject
items.example: She was brought up by her grandparents.

items.meaning: to return something; to make you remember something
items.example: This song brings back so many memories.

items.meaning: to cause something to happen
items.example: The internet brought about huge changes in our lives.

items.meaning: to reduce something; to make a government lose power
items.example: The new law should bring down prices.

items.meaning: to move an event to an earlier date or time
items.example: The meeting has been brought forward to Monday.

items.meaning: to introduce a new law or system
items.example: The government brought in a new tax on sugar.

items.meaning: to start a business or organisation; to arrange something
items.example: She set up her own company at 25.

items.meaning: to start a journey
items.example: We set off early to avoid the traffic.

items.meaning: to delay something or make it slower
items.example: The bad weather set the project back by two weeks.

items.meaning: to keep something, especially money or time, for a special purpose
items.example: I set aside some money every month for holidays.

items.meaning: to invent a story or excuse; to become friends again after an argument
items.example: He made up an excuse for being late.

items.meaning: to do something good to correct something bad you did before
items.example: I bought her flowers to make up for forgetting her birthday.

items.meaning: to see, hear or understand something with difficulty
items.example: I couldn't make out what he was saying.

items.meaning: to do or eat less of something
items.example: I'm trying to cut down on sugar.

items.meaning: to stop the supply of something; to interrupt a phone call
items.example: They cut off our electricity because we didn't pay.

items.meaning: to stop eating or doing something completely; to remove something
items.example: The doctor told him to cut out alcohol.

items.meaning: to interrupt someone who is speaking
items.example: Sorry to cut in, but we need to leave.

items.meaning: to fall to the ground
items.example: The little boy fell down and started crying.

items.meaning: to fail to do something as fast as other people or as planned
items.example: I was ill for two weeks and fell behind at school.

items.meaning: to stop being friends with someone after an argument
items.example: She fell out with her best friend over money.

items.meaning: to break into pieces; to stop working well
items.example: My old shoes are falling apart.

items.meaning: to believe a trick or a lie; to fall in love with someone
items.example: I can't believe you fell for that old trick!

items.meaning: (a plan or deal) to fail to happen
items.example: Our plans for the trip fell through.

items.meaning: to continue doing something
items.example: Carry on with your work while I'm out.

items.meaning: to do a task, test or plan
items.example: The scientists carried out an experiment.

items.meaning: to continue doing something, often in an annoying way
items.example: He keeps on asking the same question.

items.meaning: to stay at the same level or speed as someone or something
items.translation: seguir el ritmo de / estar al día
items.example: I can't keep up with all the new apps.

items.meaning: to wait for a short time (often on the phone)
items.example: Hold on, I'll get a pen.

items.meaning: to delay someone or something
items.example: Sorry I'm late, I was held up in traffic.

items.meaning: to phone someone again or phone someone who called you
items.example: I'm busy now, can I call you back?

items.meaning: to cancel an event or plan
items.example: They called off the match because of the rain.

items.meaning: to need or demand something
items.example: This situation calls for quick action.

items.meaning: to arrive and register at a hotel or airport
items.example: We checked in at the hotel at three.

items.meaning: to pay and leave a hotel
items.translation: dejar el hotel / hacer el check-out
items.example: We have to check out before eleven.

items.meaning: to complete a form with information
items.example: Please fill in this form.

items.meaning: to make something completely full
items.example: Fill up the tank before the trip.

items.meaning: to discover information or a fact
items.example: I need to find out what time the train leaves.

items.meaning: to exercise; to find the answer to a problem
items.example: Don't worry, we'll work it out together.

items.meaning: to spend time improving or doing something
items.example: I need to work on my pronunciation.

items.meaning: to put something in the rubbish
items.example: Don't throw away those boxes, I need them.

items.meaning: to vomit
items.example: I felt so sick that I threw up.

items.meaning: to arrive, especially late or unexpectedly
items.example: He showed up an hour late.

items.meaning: to try to impress people with what you have or can do
items.example: Stop showing off with your new car!

items.meaning: to change from a child into an adult
items.example: I grew up in a small village.

items.meaning: to become too big for clothes; to stop doing something as you get older
items.example: My son has grown out of all his shoes.

items.meaning: to spend time somewhere or with someone, relaxing
items.example: We usually hang out at the park after school.

items.meaning: to end a phone call
items.example: She was so angry that she hung up on me.

items.meaning: to wait for a short time
items.example: Hang on a minute, I'm almost ready.

items.meaning: to put on clothes to see if they fit
items.example: Can I try on these jeans?

items.meaning: to test something to see if it works or if you like it
items.example: I want to try out the new pizza place.

items.meaning: to allow someone to enter
items.example: Who let you in? The door was locked.

items.meaning: to disappoint someone by not doing what you promised
items.example: I promised to help and I won't let you down.

items.meaning: to not punish someone, or give them a light punishment
items.example: The police officer let him off with a warning.

items.meaning: to die (a polite way of saying it)
items.example: His grandfather passed away last year.

items.meaning: to give a message or object to another person
items.example: Can you pass on the message to Sarah?

items.meaning: to become unconscious
items.example: It was so hot that two people passed out.

items.meaning: to take someone or something to a place and leave them there; to fall asleep
items.translation: dejar (a alguien en un sitio) / quedarse dormido
items.example: I'll drop you off at school on my way to work.

items.meaning: to visit someone briefly, without planning
items.example: Drop by the office tomorrow and pick up the keys.

items.meaning: to leave school or a course before finishing it
items.example: He dropped out of university after one year.
